review: The hymn is the nativity in the church's question-and-answer form: 1:1–4 asks why light and song broke into the night, 2:1–3 is Luke 2:14 quoted exactly (כָּבוֹד לֵאלֹהִים בַּמָּרוֹם … רָצוֹן), 3:1–4 2 Cor 8:9 with Phil 2:7, 4:1–4 Gal 4:4 (בַּמּוֹעֵד) with John 1:29 and 19:30, and 5:1–4 1 Cor 15:4–5, 6:1–4 Phil 2:9–10.

1:2 מַדּוּעַ בַּלַּיְלָה אוֹר — the Arabic لِمَ ضَاءَ اللَّيْلَ نُور is a question, not a statement; the Hebrew keeps the interrogative מַדּוּעַ in both 1:2 and 1:3 so the stanza still reads as the catechism's two questions and not as a narration of the shepherds' night.

2:3 רָצוֹן גַּם־לִבְנֵי הָאָדָם — the Arabic بِالنَّاسِ أَيْضًا سُرُور is the Byzantine 'good pleasure in men'; the Hebrew uses רָצוֹן, the noun Luke 2:14 itself uses (ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκίας), rather than שָׂשׂוֹן, so the line is the angelic word and not a comment on it.

3:4 אָדוֹן בְּתוֹךְ עֲבָדִים — the Arabic سَيِّدًا وَسْطَ الْعَبِيد is the stanza's paradox; עֶבֶד is kept even though it sounds harsh, because the argument needs the real servile word and not the softer מְשָׁרֵת.

6:2 מַעֲלָה רָמָה — the Arabic أَسْمَى مَقَام is 'the loftiest station'; the Hebrew uses the concrete 'a high step/degree' rather than the abstract מַעֲמָד, since the line is about the ascension's place at the right hand and the stanza should end on height, not on rank.
